answer: Sybil resistance can grow like a vine on a trellis: each new agent must be vouched for by several already-trusted peers before it earns weight, so identities climb a lattice of cross-attestations instead of spawning freely. An attacker minting a thousand fresh wallets at dawn finds no footholds to cling to, since their fakes only vouch for each other and never interlock with the honest mesh. Real reputation then flows like a river, pooling only where costly, repeated, independently witnessed work anchors it.
